Remark
[Riemannian normal coordinates]

Source: petersen:page-0206 ↗ def:pet-ch5-injectivity-radius

Identifying $T_pM$ with $\mathbb R^n$ via a linear isomorphism and using that $\exp _p$ is a diffeomorphism near $0$ gives exponential or Riemannian normal coordinates at $p$, unique up to the choice of identification; requiring a linear isometry makes them unique up to $O(n)$. Part (2) of subsection 5.1 says that points $q_1,q_2$ sufficiently near $p$ are joined by a unique short geodesic $\exp _{q_1}(tv)$, $|v|$ small.
